passages.text: Then it was reported to Joab, “The king is weeping and mourning over Absalom.”
passages.sermon:
Joab was a commander in King David’s army.
Someone told Joab important news.
The person said, “Look, the king is crying.”
The person also said, “The king is mourning for Absalom.”
passages.original: וַיֻּגַּ֖ד לְיוֹאָ֑ב הִנֵּ֨ה הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ בֹּכֶ֛ה וַיִּתְאַבֵּ֖ל עַל־ אַבְשָׁלֹֽם׃

passages.text: And that day’s victory was turned into mourning for all the people, because on that day they were told, “The king is grieving over his son.”
passages.sermon:
The people won a victory that day.
But the victory became a time of mourning for everyone.
The people heard news that day.
They heard, “The king is grieving over his son.”
This news turned their joy into sorrow.
passages.original: וַתְּהִ֨י הַתְּשֻׁעָ֜ה בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֛וּא לְאֵ֖בֶל לְכָל־ הָעָ֑ם כִּֽי־ שָׁמַ֣ע הָעָ֗ם בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר נֶעֱצַ֥ב הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ עַל־ בְּנֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So they returned to the city quietly that day, as people steal away in humiliation after fleeing a battle.
passages.sermon:
The people returned to the city that day.
They moved quietly.
They felt ashamed.
They acted like people who run away from battle.
They did not celebrate.
They entered the city in silence.
passages.original: וַיִּתְגַּנֵּ֥ב הָעָ֛ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא לָב֣וֹא הָעִ֑יר כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יִתְגַּנֵּ֗ב הָעָם֙ הַנִּכְלָמִ֔ים בְּנוּסָ֖ם בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

passages.text: But the king covered his face and cried out at the top of his voice, “O my son Absalom! O Absalom, my son, my son!”
passages.sermon:
The king was David.
David was grieving for his son Absalom.
David covered his face.
David cried out loudly.
David said, “My son Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!”
passages.original: וְהַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ לָאַ֣ט אֶת־ פָּנָ֔יו וַיִּזְעַ֥ק הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ ק֣וֹל גָּד֑וֹל בְּנִי֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם בְּנִ֥י בְנִֽי׃ס

passages.text: Then Joab went into the house and said to the king, “Today you have disgraced all your servants who have saved your life and the lives of your sons and daughters, of your wives, and of your concubines.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of King David’s army.
Joab went into the house where King David was.
Joab spoke to King David.
Joab said, “Today you have disgraced all your servants.”
These servants saved your life today.
They also saved the lives of your sons and your daughters.
They saved the lives of your wives.
They saved the lives of your concubines.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֥א יוֹאָ֛ב אֶל־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ הַבָּ֑יִת וַיֹּאמֶר֩ הֹבַ֨שְׁתָּ הַיּ֜וֹם אֶת־ פְּנֵ֣י כָל־ עֲבָדֶ֗יךָ הַֽמְמַלְּטִ֤ים אֶֽת־ נַפְשְׁךָ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם וְאֵ֨ת נֶ֤פֶשׁ בָּנֶ֙יךָ֙ וּבְנֹתֶ֔יךָ וְנֶ֣פֶשׁ נָשֶׁ֔יךָ וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ פִּלַגְשֶֽׁיךָ׃

passages.text: You love those who hate you and hate those who love you! For you have made it clear today that the commanders and soldiers mean nothing to you. I know today that if Absalom were alive and all of us were dead, it would have pleased you!
passages.sermon:
Joab spoke to King David.
Joab said, “You love those who hate you.
You hate those who love you.
Today you have shown that your commanders and your servants mean nothing to you.
I know this today.
If Absalom were alive today, and all of us were dead, you would be pleased.”
passages.original: לְאַֽהֲבָה֙ אֶת־ שֹׂ֣נְאֶ֔יךָ וְלִשְׂנֹ֖א אֶת־ אֹהֲבֶ֑יךָ כִּ֣י׀ הִגַּ֣דְתָּ הַיּ֗וֹם כִּ֣י אֵ֤ין לְךָ֙ שָׂרִ֣ים וַעֲבָדִ֔ים כִּ֣י׀ יָדַ֣עְתִּי הַיּ֗וֹם כִּ֠י לֹא אַבְשָׁל֥וֹם חַי֙ וְכֻלָּ֤נוּ הַיּוֹם֙ מֵתִ֔ים כִּי־ אָ֖ז יָשָׁ֥ר בְּעֵינֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Now therefore get up! Go out and speak comfort to your servants, for I swear by the LORD that if you do not go out, not a man will remain with you tonight. This will be worse for you than all the adversity that has befallen you from your youth until now!”
passages.sermon:
Joab spoke to King David.
Joab told David what to do.
Joab said, “Get up now.
Go out to your servants.
Speak kindly to your servants.
I swear this by the LORD.
If you do not go out,
No one will stay with you tonight.
This trouble will be worse for you than any trouble you have had.
You have faced trouble since you were young until now.
This will be the worst of all if you do not act.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּה֙ ק֣וּם צֵ֔א וְדַבֵּ֖ר עַל־ לֵ֣ב עֲבָדֶ֑יךָ כִּי֩ בַיהוָ֨ה נִשְׁבַּ֜עְתִּי כִּי־ אֵינְךָ֣ יוֹצֵ֗א אִם־ יָלִ֨ין אִ֤ישׁ אִתְּךָ֙ הַלַּ֔יְלָה וְרָעָ֧ה לְךָ֣ זֹ֗את מִכָּל־ הָרָעָה֙ אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֣אָה עָלֶ֔יךָ מִנְּעֻרֶ֖יךָ עַד־ עָֽתָּה׃ס

passages.text: So the king got up and sat in the gate, and all the people were told: “Behold, the king is sitting in the gate.” So they all came before the king. Meanwhile, the Israelites had fled, each man to his home.
passages.sermon:
King David got up.
He sat in the gate of the city.
People told everyone, “Look, the king is sitting in the gate.”
All the people came and stood before King David.
At the same time, the Israelites had fled.
Each man went to his own home.
passages.original: וַיָּ֥קָם הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב בַּשָּׁ֑עַר וּֽלְכָל־ הָעָ֞ם הִגִּ֣ידוּ לֵאמֹ֗ר הִנֵּ֤ה הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב בַּשַּׁ֔עַר וַיָּבֹ֤א כָל־ הָעָם֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נָ֖ס אִ֥ישׁ לְאֹהָלָֽיו׃ס

passages.text: And all the people throughout the tribes of Israel were arguing, “The king rescued us from the hand of our enemies and delivered us from the hand of the Philistines, but now he has fled the land because of Absalom.
passages.sermon:
All the people in Israel spoke together.
They spoke in every tribe.
They said, “The king saved us from our enemies.
He rescued us from the Philistines.
Now the king has left the land.
He fled because of Absalom.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֤י כָל־ הָעָם֙ נָד֔וֹן בְּכָל־ שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ הִצִּילָ֣נוּ׀ מִכַּ֣ף אֹיְבֵ֗ינוּ וְה֤וּא מִלְּטָ֙נוּ֙ מִכַּ֣ף פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְעַתָּ֛ה בָּרַ֥ח מִן־ הָאָ֖רֶץ מֵעַ֥ל אַבְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: But Absalom, the man we anointed over us, has died in battle. So why do you say nothing about restoring the king?”
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the man we anointed to rule over us.
Absalom has died in battle.
Now the king is not ruling.
You are saying nothing about bringing the king back.
Why are you silent about restoring the king?
passages.original: וְאַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָשַׁ֣חְנוּ עָלֵ֔ינוּ מֵ֖ת בַּמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וְעַתָּ֗ה לָמָ֥ה אַתֶּ֛ם מַחֲרִשִׁ֖ים לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֶת־ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס

passages.text: Then King David sent this message to Zadok and Abiathar, the priests: “Say to the elders of Judah, ‘Why should you be the last to restore the king to his palace, since the talk of all Israel has reached the king at his quarters?
passages.sermon:
King David was the ruler of Israel.
David sent a message to Zadok and Abiathar.
Zadok and Abiathar were priests.
David told them to speak to the elders of Judah.
David said, “Why are you the last to bring the king back to his house?”
All Israel has already spoken to the king at his house.
passages.original: וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֗ד שָׁ֠לַח אֶל־ צָד֨וֹק וְאֶל־ אֶבְיָתָ֥ר הַכֹּהֲנִים֮ לֵאמֹר֒ דַּבְּר֞וּ אֶל־ זִקְנֵ֤י יְהוּדָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לָ֤מָּה תִֽהְיוּ֙ אַֽחֲרֹנִ֔ים לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֶת־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־ בֵּית֑וֹ וּדְבַר֙ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בָּ֥א אֶל־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־ בֵּיתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: You are my brothers, my own flesh and blood. So why should you be the last to restore the king?’
passages.sermon:
King David spoke to the elders of Judah.
He said, "You are my brothers."
You are my own flesh and blood.
Why should you be the last to bring back the king?"
passages.original: אַחַ֣י אַתֶּ֔ם עַצְמִ֥י וּבְשָׂרִ֖י אַתֶּ֑ם וְלָ֧מָּה תִהְי֛וּ אַחֲרֹנִ֖ים לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֶת־ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: And say to Amasa, ‘Aren’t you my flesh and blood? May God punish me, and ever so severely, if from this time you are not the commander of my army in place of Joab!’ ”
passages.sermon:
King David spoke to Amasa.
Amasa was his relative.
David said, "You are my own flesh and blood."
David made a promise to Amasa.
David said, "May God punish me if I do not make you commander of my army."
David said, "You will be commander instead of Joab."
David said, "You will be commander before me for all days from now on."
passages.original: וְלַֽעֲמָשָׂא֙ תֹּֽמְר֔וּ הֲל֛וֹא עַצְמִ֥י וּבְשָׂרִ֖י אָ֑תָּה כֹּ֣ה יַֽעֲשֶׂה־ לִּ֤י אֱלֹהִים֙ וְכֹ֣ה יוֹסִ֔יף אִם־ לֹ֠א שַׂר־ צָבָ֞א תִּהְיֶ֧ה לְפָנַ֛י כָּל־ הַיָּמִ֖ים תַּ֥חַת יוֹאָֽב׃

passages.text: So he swayed the hearts of all the men of Judah as though they were one man, and they sent word to the king: “Return, you and all your servants.”
passages.sermon:
David spoke to the men of Judah.
He persuaded their hearts.
All the men of Judah agreed together.
They became united in purpose.
They sent a message to King David.
They said, “Return, you and all your servants.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֛ט אֶת־ לְבַ֥ב כָּל־ אִישׁ־ יְהוּדָ֖ה כְּאִ֣ישׁ אֶחָ֑ד וַֽיִּשְׁלְחוּ֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ שׁ֥וּב אַתָּ֖ה וְכָל־ עֲבָדֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: So the king returned, and when he arrived at the Jordan, the men of Judah came to Gilgal to meet him and escort him across the Jordan.
passages.sermon:
King David returned.
He came to the Jordan River.
The men of Judah went to Gilgal.
They went to meet King David.
They came to escort King David across the Jordan River.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣שָׁב הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיָּבֹ֖א עַד־ הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן וִיהוּדָ֞ה בָּ֣א הַגִּלְגָּ֗לָה לָלֶ֙כֶת֙ לִקְרַ֣את הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לְהַעֲבִ֥יר אֶת־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶת־ הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

passages.text: Then Shimei son of Gera, a Benjamite from Bahurim, hurried down with the men of Judah to meet King David, along with a thousand men of Benjamin, as well as Ziba the steward of the house of Saul and his fifteen sons and twenty servants. They rushed down to the Jordan before the king and crossed at the ford to carry over the king’s household and to do what was good in his sight. When Shimei son of Gera crossed the Jordan, he fell down before the king and said, “My lord, do not hold me guilty, and do not remember your servant’s wrongdoing on the day my lord the king left Jerusalem. May the king not take it to heart.
passages.sermon:
Shimei was the son of Gera.
Shimei was a Benjamite from Bahurim.
Shimei hurried down with the men of Judah.
They went to meet King David.
A thousand men of Benjamin went with Shimei.
Ziba also went with them.
Ziba was the steward of the house of Saul.
Ziba brought his fifteen sons and twenty servants.
They all rushed down to the Jordan before the king.
They crossed at the ford.
They came to carry over the king’s household.
They wanted to do what was good in the king’s sight.
Shimei son of Gera crossed the Jordan.
Shimei fell down before the king.
Shimei spoke to the king.
He said, “My lord, do not hold me guilty.
Do not remember your servant’s wrongdoing.
I sinned on the day my lord the king left Jerusalem.
Please do not take it to heart.”
passages.original: וַיְמַהֵ֗ר שִׁמְעִ֤י בֶן־ גֵּרָא֙ בֶּן־ הַיְמִינִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֖ר מִבַּֽחוּרִ֑ים וַיֵּ֙רֶד֙ עִם־ אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה לִקְרַ֖את הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ דָּוִֽד׃ וְאֶ֨לֶף אִ֣ישׁ עִמּוֹ֮ מִבִּנְיָמִן֒ וְצִיבָ֗א נַ֚עַר בֵּ֣ית שָׁא֔וּל וַחֲמֵ֨שֶׁת עָשָׂ֥ר בָּנָ֛יו וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים עֲבָדָ֖יו אִתּ֑וֹ וְצָלְח֥וּ הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ וְעָבְרָ֣ה הָעֲבָרָ֗ה לַֽעֲבִיר֙ אֶת־ בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְלַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הַטּ֖וֹב בְּעֵינוֹ וְשִׁמְעִ֣י בֶן־ גֵּרָ֗א נָפַל֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ בְּעָבְר֖וֹ בַּיַּרְדֵּֽן׃ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל־ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אַל־ יַחֲשָׁב־ לִ֣י אֲדֹנִי֮ עָוֺן֒ וְאַל־ תִּזְכֹּ֗ר אֵ֚ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶעֱוָ֣ה עַבְדְּךָ֔ בַּיּ֕וֹם אֲשֶׁר־ יָׄצָ֥ׄאׄ אֲדֹנִֽי־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מִירֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לָשׂ֥וּם הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־ לִבּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: For your servant knows that I have sinned, so here I am today as the first of all the house of Joseph to come down to meet my lord the king.”
passages.sermon:
Shimei son of Gera is speaking to King David.
Shimei is a Benjamite from Bahurim.
Shimei says he is David’s servant.
Shimei says he knows he has sinned.
Shimei says he has come today.
Shimei says he is the first from all the house of Joseph to come.
Shimei says he has come down to meet his lord, the king.
passages.original: כִּ֚י יָדַ֣ע עַבְדְּךָ֔ כִּ֖י אֲנִ֣י חָטָ֑אתִי וְהִנֵּֽה־ בָ֣אתִי הַיּ֗וֹם רִאשׁוֹן֙ לְכָל־ בֵּ֣ית יוֹסֵ֔ף לָרֶ֕דֶת לִקְרַ֖את אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס

passages.text: But Abishai son of Zeruiah said, “Shouldn’t Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the LORD’s anointed?”
passages.sermon:
Abishai was the son of Zeruiah.
Abishai spoke to King David.
Abishai asked a question about Shimei.
Abishai said, “Should Shimei not be put to death for this?”
Abishai explained his reason.
Abishai said, “Shimei cursed the LORD’s anointed.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֨עַן אֲבִישַׁ֤י בֶּן־ צְרוּיָה֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר הֲתַ֣חַת זֹ֔את לֹ֥א יוּמַ֖ת שִׁמְעִ֑י כִּ֥י קִלֵּ֖ל אֶת־ מְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: And David replied, “Sons of Zeruiah, what have I to do with you, that you should be my adversaries today? Should any man be put to death in Israel today? Am I not indeed aware that today I am king over Israel?”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David spoke to the sons of Zeruiah.
David said, “What do I have to do with you?”
David said, “You are acting as my adversaries today.”
David said, “Should anyone be put to death in Israel today?”
David said, “I know that today I am king over Israel.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗ד מַה־ לִּ֤י וְלָכֶם֙ בְּנֵ֣י צְרוּיָ֔ה כִּי־ תִֽהְיוּ־ לִ֥י הַיּ֖וֹם לְשָׂטָ֑ן הַיּ֗וֹם י֤וּמַת אִישׁ֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֚י הֲל֣וֹא יָדַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֥י הַיּ֖וֹם אֲנִי־ מֶ֥לֶךְ עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: So the king said to Shimei, “You shall not die.” And the king swore an oath to him.
passages.sermon:
King David spoke to Shimei.
David said, “You will not die.”
David made an oath to Shimei.
David promised to spare Shimei’s life.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אֶל־ שִׁמְעִ֖י לֹ֣א תָמ֑וּת וַיִּשָּׁ֥בַֽע ל֖וֹ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס

passages.text: Then Mephibosheth, Saul’s grandson, went down to meet the king. He had not cared for his feet or trimmed his mustache or washed his clothes from the day the king had left until the day he returned safely.
passages.sermon:
Mephibosheth was Saul’s grandson.
He went down to meet the king.
Mephibosheth had not cared for his feet.
He had not trimmed his mustache.
He had not washed his clothes.
He did not do these things from the day the king left.
He continued this until the day the king returned safely.
passages.original: וּמְפִבֹ֙שֶׁת֙ בֶּן־ שָׁא֔וּל יָרַ֖ד לִקְרַ֣את הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְלֹא־ עָשָׂ֨ה רַגְלָ֜יו וְלֹא־ עָשָׂ֣ה שְׂפָמ֗וֹ וְאֶת־ בְּגָדָיו֙ לֹ֣א כִבֵּ֔ס לְמִן־ הַיּוֹם֙ לֶ֣כֶת הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עַד־ הַיּ֖וֹם אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֥א בְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: And he came from Jerusalem to meet the king, who asked him, “Mephibosheth, why did you not go with me?”
passages.sermon:
Mephibosheth was Saul’s grandson.
He lived in Jerusalem.
The king returned to Jerusalem.
Mephibosheth went out to meet the king.
The king saw Mephibosheth.
The king spoke to Mephibosheth.
The king asked, “Mephibosheth, why did you not go with me?”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֛י כִּי־ בָ֥א יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם לִקְרַ֣את הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לָ֛מָּה לֹא־ הָלַ֥כְתָּ עִמִּ֖י מְפִיבֹֽשֶׁת׃

passages.text: “My lord the king,” he replied, “because I am lame, I said, ‘I will have my donkey saddled so that I may ride on it and go with the king.’ But my servant Ziba deceived me, and he has slandered your servant to my lord the king. Yet my lord the king is like the angel of God, so do what is good in your eyes.
passages.sermon:
Mephibosheth was Saul’s grandson.
Mephibosheth spoke to King David.
Mephibosheth said, “My lord the king, my servant Ziba deceived me.”
Mephibosheth said, “I am lame.”
Mephibosheth said, “I told my servant, ‘Saddle the donkey for me.’”
Mephibosheth said, “I wanted to ride on the donkey and go with the king.”
Mephibosheth said, “But Ziba tricked me.”
Mephibosheth said, “Ziba slandered me to you, my lord the king.”
Mephibosheth said, “My lord the king is like the angel of God.”
Mephibosheth said, “Do what is good in your eyes.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמַ֕ר אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ עַבְדִּ֣י רִמָּ֑נִי כִּֽי־ אָמַ֨ר עַבְדְּךָ֜ אֶחְבְּשָׁה־ לִּי֩ הַחֲמ֨וֹר וְאֶרְכַּ֤ב עָלֶ֙יהָ֙ וְאֵלֵ֣ךְ אֶת־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּ֥י פִסֵּ֖חַ עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃ וַיְרַגֵּ֣ל בְּעַבְדְּךָ֔ אֶל־ אֲדֹנִ֖י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַאדֹנִ֤י הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ כְּמַלְאַ֣ךְ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַעֲשֵׂ֥ה הַטּ֖וֹב בְּעֵינֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: For all the house of my grandfather deserves death from my lord the king, yet you have set your servant among those who eat at your table. What further right, then, do I have to keep appealing to the king?”
passages.sermon:
Mephibosheth spoke to King David.
Mephibosheth said his whole family deserved death from the king.
Mephibosheth called himself the king’s servant.
Mephibosheth said the king let him eat at the royal table.
Mephibosheth asked what right he had to ask the king for anything more.
Mephibosheth said he had no more reason to appeal to the king.
passages.original: כִּי֩ לֹ֨א הָיָ֜ה כָּל־ בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֗י כִּ֤י אִם־ אַנְשֵׁי־ מָ֙וֶת֙ לַאדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַתָּ֙שֶׁת֙ אֶֽת־ עַבְדְּךָ֔ בְּאֹכְלֵ֖י שֻׁלְחָנֶ֑ךָ וּמַה־ יֶּשׁ־ לִ֥י עוֹד֙ צְדָקָ֔ה וְלִזְעֹ֥ק ע֖וֹד אֶל־ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃פ

passages.text: The king replied, “Why say any more? I hereby declare that you and Ziba are to divide the land.”
passages.sermon:
King David spoke to Mephibosheth.
King David was the ruler of Israel.
King David said, “Why do you keep speaking?”
King David said, “I have made my decision.”
King David said, “You and Ziba must divide the land.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לָ֛מָּה תְּדַבֵּ֥ר ע֖וֹד דְּבָרֶ֑יךָ אָמַ֕רְתִּי אַתָּ֣ה וְצִיבָ֔א תַּחְלְק֖וּ אֶת־ הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃

passages.text: And Mephibosheth said to the king, “Instead, since my lord the king has safely come to his own house, let Ziba take it all!”
passages.sermon:
Mephibosheth was the son of Jonathan and the grandson of Saul.
He was lame in both feet.
He had been shown kindness by King David.
Mephibosheth spoke to King David.
He said, “Let Ziba take everything.”
He said this because King David had returned home safely.
Mephibosheth cared most that the king had come back in peace.
He did not care about the land or possessions.
He wanted the king’s safety above all else.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מְפִיבֹ֙שֶׁת֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ גַּ֥ם אֶת־ הַכֹּ֖ל יִקָּ֑ח אַ֠חֲרֵי אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֞א אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֛לֶך בְּשָׁל֖וֹם אֶל־ בֵּיתֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: Now Barzillai the Gileadite had come down from Rogelim to cross the Jordan with the king and send him on his way from there.
passages.sermon:
Barzillai was a Gileadite.
Barzillai lived in Rogelim.
Barzillai came down from Rogelim.
Barzillai came to the Jordan River.
The king was at the Jordan River.
Barzillai crossed the Jordan River with the king.
Barzillai wanted to send the king on his way from the Jordan River.
passages.original: וּבַרְזִלַּי֙ הַגִּלְעָדִ֔י יָרַ֖ד מֵרֹגְלִ֑ים וַיַּעֲבֹ֤ר אֶת־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן לְשַׁלְּח֖וֹ אֶת־ בַּיַּרְדֵּן׃

passages.text: Barzillai was quite old, eighty years of age, and since he was a very wealthy man, he had provided for the king while he stayed in Mahanaim.
passages.sermon:
Barzillai was a man from Gilead.
He was very old.
He was eighty years old.
Barzillai was very wealthy.
He provided for King David.
He gave for the king’s needs while David stayed in Mahanaim.
passages.original: וּבַרְזִלַּי֙ זָקֵ֣ן מְאֹ֔ד בֶּן־ שְׁמֹנִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה וְהֽוּא־ כִלְכַּ֤ל אֶת־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ בְּשִׁיבָת֣וֹ בְמַחֲנַ֔יִם כִּֽי־ אִ֛ישׁ גָּד֥וֹל ה֖וּא מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: The king said to Barzillai, “Cross over with me, and I will provide for you at my side in Jerusalem.”
passages.sermon:
The king spoke to Barzillai.
Barzillai was a very old and wealthy man.
Barzillai had helped the king while the king stayed in Mahanaim.
The king said, "Come with me."
The king said, "Cross the Jordan with me."
The king said, "I will take care of you in Jerusalem."
The king said, "You will be with me at my side."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־ בַּרְזִלָּ֑י אַתָּה֙ עֲבֹ֣ר אִתִּ֔י וְכִלְכַּלְתִּ֥י אֹתְךָ֛ עִמָּדִ֖י בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: But Barzillai replied, “How many years of my life remain, that I should go up to Jerusalem with the king?
passages.sermon:
Barzillai was a very old man.
He was eighty years old.
Barzillai had provided for King David while David stayed in Mahanaim.
Barzillai was very wealthy.
The king invited Barzillai to cross over with him to Jerusalem.
The king promised to provide for Barzillai in Jerusalem.
Barzillai replied to the king.
Barzillai said, "How many years of my life remain?"
Barzillai asked, "Why should I go up to Jerusalem with the king?"
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר בַּרְזִלַּ֖י אֶל־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ כַּמָּ֗ה יְמֵי֙ שְׁנֵ֣י חַיַּ֔י כִּי־ אֶעֱלֶ֥ה אֶת־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: I am now eighty years old. Can I discern what is good and what is not? Can your servant taste what he eats or drinks? Can I still hear the voice of singing men and women? Why should your servant be an added burden to my lord the king?
passages.sermon:
Barzillai was an old man.
Barzillai was eighty years old.
Barzillai spoke to King David.
Barzillai said, “I am now eighty years old.”
Barzillai asked, “Can I know what is good and what is bad?”
Barzillai asked, “Can your servant taste what he eats?”
Barzillai asked, “Can your servant taste what he drinks?”
Barzillai asked, “Can I still hear the voices of men who sing?”
Barzillai asked, “Can I still hear the voices of women who sing?”
Barzillai asked, “Why should your servant be a burden to my lord the king?”
passages.original: בֶּן־ שְׁמֹנִ֣ים שָׁנָה֩ אָנֹכִ֨י הַיּ֜וֹם הַאֵדַ֣ע׀ בֵּין־ ט֣וֹב לְרָ֗ע אִם־ יִטְעַ֤ם עַבְדְּךָ֙ אֶת־ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֹכַל֙ וְאֶת־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶשְׁתֶּ֔ה אִם־ אֶשְׁמַ֣ע ע֔וֹד בְּק֖וֹל שָׁרִ֣ים וְשָׁר֑וֹת וְלָמָּה֩ יִֽהְיֶ֨ה עַבְדְּךָ֥ עוֹד֙ לְמַשָּׂ֔א אֶל־ אֲדֹנִ֖י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: Your servant could go with the king only a short distance past the Jordan; why should the king repay me with such a reward?
passages.sermon:
Barzillai spoke to King David.
Barzillai was an old man.
Barzillai said he could only go a short distance with the king.
Barzillai could cross the Jordan River with the king, but not farther.
Barzillai asked why the king should reward him so greatly.
Barzillai wondered why he deserved such a reward from the king.
passages.original: כִּמְעַ֞ט יַעֲבֹ֧ר עַבְדְּךָ֛ אֶת־ הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן אֶת־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְלָ֙מָּה֙ יִגְמְלֵ֣נִי הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הַגְּמוּלָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

passages.text: Please let your servant return, that I may die in my own city near the tomb of my father and mother. But here is your servant Chimham. Let him cross over with my lord the king, and do for him what is good in your sight.”
passages.sermon:
Barzillai was an old man.
Barzillai spoke to King David.
Barzillai said, "Please let your servant return home."
I want to die in my own city.
I want to be buried near the tomb of my father and mother.
Here is your servant Chimham.
Let Chimham cross over with my lord the king.
Do for Chimham what is good in your sight.
passages.original: יָֽשָׁב־ נָ֤א עַבְדְּךָ֙ וְאָמֻ֣ת בְּעִירִ֔י עִ֛ם קֶ֥בֶר אָבִ֖י וְאִמִּ֑י וְהִנֵּ֣ה׀ עַבְדְּךָ֣ כִמְהָ֗ם יַֽעֲבֹר֙ עִם־ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַעֲשֵׂה־ ל֕וֹ אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־ ט֖וֹב בְּעֵינֶֽיךָ׃ס

passages.text: The king replied, “Chimham will cross over with me, and I will do for him what seems good in your sight, and I will do for you whatever you desire of me.”
passages.sermon:
King David spoke.
He said, “Chimham will cross the Jordan with me.
I will do for Chimham what you think is good.
I will also do for you whatever you ask of me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אִתִּי֙ יַעֲבֹ֣ר כִּמְהָ֔ם וַאֲנִי֙ אֶעֱשֶׂה־ לּ֔וֹ אֶת־ הַטּ֖וֹב בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ וְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־ תִּבְחַ֥ר עָלַ֖י אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־ לָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: So all the people crossed the Jordan, and then the king crossed over. The king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and Barzillai returned home.
passages.sermon:
All the people crossed the Jordan River.
The king also crossed the Jordan River.
The king kissed Barzillai.
The king blessed Barzillai.
Barzillai returned to his home.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲבֹ֧ר כָּל־ הָעָ֛ם אֶת־ הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ עָבָ֑ר וַיִּשַּׁ֨ק הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ לְבַרְזִלַּי֙ וַיְבָ֣רֲכֵ֔הוּ וַיָּ֖שָׁב לִמְקֹמֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: Then the king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham crossed over with him. All the troops of Judah and half the troops of Israel escorted the king.
passages.sermon:
The king went to Gilgal.
Chimham went with the king.
All the people of Judah escorted the king.
Half the people of Israel also escorted the king.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲבֹ֤ר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ הַגִּלְגָּ֔לָה וְכִמְהָ֖ן עָבַ֣ר עִמּ֑וֹ וְכָל־ עַ֤ם יְהוּדָה֙ וַיַּעֲבִרוּ אֶת־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְגַ֕ם חֲצִ֖י עַ֥ם יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Soon all the men of Israel came to the king and asked, “Why did our brothers, the men of Judah, take you away secretly and bring the king and his household across the Jordan, together with all of David’s men?”
passages.sermon:
All the men of Israel came to the king.
They spoke to the king.
They asked a question.
They said, “Why did our brothers, the men of Judah, take you away in secret?
Why did they bring you, the king, and your household across the Jordan?
Why did they bring all of David’s men with you?”
passages.original: וְהִנֵּ֛ה כָּל־ אִ֥ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּאִ֣ים אֶל־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ מַדּוּעַ֩ גְּנָב֨וּךָ אַחֵ֜ינוּ אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֗ה וַיַּעֲבִ֨רוּ אֶת־ הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ וְאֶת־ בֵּיתוֹ֙ אֶת־ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וְכָל־ אַנְשֵׁ֥י דָוִ֖ד עִמּֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: And all the men of Judah replied to the men of Israel, “We did this because the king is our relative. Why does this anger you? Have we ever eaten at the king’s expense or received anything for ourselves?”
passages.sermon:
All the men of Judah answered the men of Israel.
They said, “The king is our relative.
That is why we did this.
Why are you angry about this?
We have not eaten at the king’s expense.
We have not received anything for ourselves.”
passages.original: וַיַּעַן֩ כָּל־ אִ֨ישׁ יְהוּדָ֜ה עַל־ אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כִּֽי־ קָר֤וֹב הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֵלַ֔י וְלָ֤מָּה זֶּה֙ חָרָ֣ה לְךָ֔ עַל־ הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּ֑ה הֶאָכ֤וֹל אָכַ֙לְנוּ֙ מִן־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אִם־ נִשֵּׂ֥את נִשָּׂ֖א לָֽנוּ׃ס

passages.text: “We have ten shares in the king,” answered the men of Israel, “so we have more claim to David than you. Why then do you despise us? Were we not the first to speak of restoring our king?” But the men of Judah pressed even harder than the men of Israel.
passages.sermon:
The men of Israel spoke to the men of Judah.
The men of Israel said, “We have ten shares in the king.
We have a greater claim to David than you.
Why do you despise us?
We were the first to speak about bringing back our king.”
The men of Judah spoke more harshly than the men of Israel.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣עַן אִֽישׁ־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֩ אֶת־ אִ֨ישׁ יְהוּדָ֜ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר עֶֽשֶׂר־ יָד֨וֹת לִ֣י בַמֶּלֶךְ֮ וְגַם־ בְּדָוִד֮ אֲנִ֣י מִמְּךָ֒ וּמַדּ֙וּעַ֙ הֱקִלֹּתַ֔נִי וְלֹא־ הָיָ֨ה דְבָרִ֥י רִאשׁ֛וֹן לִ֖י לְהָשִׁ֣יב אֶת־ מַלְכִּ֑י וַיִּ֙קֶשׁ֙ דְּבַר־ אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה מִדְּבַ֖ר אִ֥ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס
